title: 2-D Shapes: Polygons, Triangles, Quadrilaterals and Circles
seo_title: Grade 6 2-D Shapes Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, visualise and name 2-D shapes in the environment and geometric settings, focusing on regular and irregular polygons (triangles, squares, rectangles, parallelograms, other quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, heptagons, octagons) and circles; similarities and differences between squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses, trapeziums and kites; describe, sort and compare 2-D shapes in terms of the length of sides, the number of sides and the size of angles.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 2-D shapes worksheets: triangles by sides and angles, quadrilaterals, diagonals and parts of a circle. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Name shapes by their sides and angles.
key_sub: A square is a special rectangle and rhombus.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Triangles by sides: equilateral, isosceles, scalene. By angles: acute-angled, right-angled, obtuse-angled.
  • Quadrilaterals: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite and trapezium. A square is a special rectangle and a special rhombus.
  • A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other.
  • Circle: diameter = 2 × radius.

Examples

Example

4 equal sides, no right angles

opposite sides parallel

Answer: a rhombus

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A square is a rectangleIt has 4 right angles.
Sides onlyLook at the angles too.
Radius or diameter?The diameter goes all the way across.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about 2-D shapes?
faq.a: Recognise, visualise and name 2-D shapes, including similarities and differences between quadrilaterals, triangles by sides and angles, and parts of a circle.
A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides next to each other.

faq.q: How many diagonals does a hexagon have?

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle. The tick marks show 3 equal sides. Pointing down does not change the name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. The 2 slanted sides have tick marks, and the base has none.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. An isosceles triangle can point down. Turning a triangle never changes its name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. It lies on its side, but 2 sides still have tick marks. An isosceles triangle can point in any direction.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: No two sides are equal, so it is a scalene triangle. There are no tick marks, so no two sides are equal.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. The 2 sides next to the right angle have tick marks. Turned or not, it is isosceles.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides. Use the tick marks.
items.e: No two sides are equal, so it is a scalene triangle. There are no tick marks, so all 3 sides are different lengths.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. Two sides are 6 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. The equal sides do not have to be the slanted ones.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: No two sides are equal, so it is a scalene triangle. The sides are 9 cm, 6 cm and 5 cm. All 3 are different.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle. All 3 sides are 8 cm.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. 100° is more than 90°. It has 2 acute angles too, but a triangle is named by its largest angle.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: All 3 angles are less than 90°, so it is an acute triangle. 60°, 50° and 70° are all less than 90°.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle. The small square shows a 90° angle. The other two angles, 40° and 50°, are acute.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. 110° is more than 90°. Pointing down does not change the name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: All 3 angles are less than 90°, so it is an acute triangle. 75°, 60° and 45° are all less than 90°.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle. The small square shows a 90° angle. The triangle is turned, but it is still a right triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is a right triangle?
items.e: Triangle A has a small square in one corner, so one angle is 90°. It is turned, but it is still a right triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is obtuse?
items.e: Triangle B has one wide angle, more than 90°. The right triangle has a 90° angle, and the other two have only acute angles.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 90°, 45° and 45°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right triangle.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 40° and 40°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so it is obtuse. Two acute angles do not make it acute: every triangle has at least 2.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides, and each pair is next to each other (not opposite). That makes it a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its sides, in order, are 8 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. The sides are not all equal (8 cm and 5 cm), so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides, and each pair is next to each other (not opposite). That makes it a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: A rectangle has all 4 sides 12 cm long. What is its best name?
items.e: It has 4 right angles (it is a rectangle) and 4 equal sides. That makes it a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm, in order around the shape. It has no parallel sides. What is its best name?
items.e: The two 5 cm sides are next to each other, and so are the two 9 cm sides. Two pairs of equal sides next to each other make a kite.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right angles, so it is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle and 4 equal sides make a rhombus. A shape with both is a square, the name that tells the most.

items.q: A quadrilateral has sides 7 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm and 4 cm (in order) and angles 70°, 110°, 70° and 110°. What is its best name?
items.e: Opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal, so it is a parallelogram. It has no right angles (not a rectangle) and its sides are not all equal (not a rhombus).

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
items.e: Exactly one pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium. Parallelograms and rhombuses have 2 pairs.

items.q: A rhombus has one right angle. What is its best name?
items.e: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal and angles next to each other add to 180°. One 90° angle makes all 4 angles 90°, so the rhombus is a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides. Its angles, in order, are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. The angles are not 90°, so it is not a square.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Its diagonals meet at E. AE = 6 cm. How long is AC?
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other in half, so E is the middle of AC. AC = 6 + 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cut each other in half. They are not equal and not at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Diagonals that cut each other in half make a parallelogram. Not equal: not a rectangle. Not at right angles: not a rhombus.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this parallelogram. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: In every parallelogram the diagonals cut each other in half. In this one they are not equal and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal, cross at right angles and cut each other in half?
items.e: Equal diagonals come from being a rectangle, and right angles where they cross come from being a rhombus. Only a square is both.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: They are not equal in length
Neither one is cut in half
They do not cross at right angles
items.e: The diagonals of this rhombus are different lengths. They do cross at right angles and cut each other in half. Only a square has equal diagonals among rhombuses.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Its diagonals meet at E. AC = 14 cm. How long is BD?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so BD = AC = 14 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this trapezium. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: This trapezium has 2 equal sides (the slanted sides), so its diagonals are equal in length. They do not cut each other in half and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cross at right angles, but only one of them is cut in half. What is it?
items.e: In a kite, the line of symmetry cuts the other diagonal in half at a right angle, but is not cut in half itself.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this kite. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: The diagonals of a kite cross at right angles. The long diagonal cuts the short one in half, but not the other way round.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Its diagonals meet at E. What is the size of angle AEB?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so angle AEB = 90°. (60° and 120° are angles of the rhombus itself.)

items.q: Andile cuts a rectangular piece of cardboard, 30 cm by 20 cm, along one diagonal. What is true about the two pieces?
items.e: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into 2 triangles with sides 30 cm, 20 cm and the diagonal. A half turn puts one exactly on the other, so they are congruent.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
items.e: A rectangle only needs 4 right angles, and every square has them. The other statements are only sometimes true.

items.q: Liam’s dad builds a deck frame. Opposite sides are 4 m and 3 m, so it is a parallelogram. He measures both diagonals: 5 m and 5 m. What does this tell him?
items.e: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle, so all 4 corners are right angles. Builders check corners this way.

items.q: Dumisani’s family builds a garden bed with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are equal. How many lines of symmetry does the garden bed have?
items.e: A trapezium with equal slanted sides has 1 line of symmetry, through the middles of the 2 parallel sides.

items.q: Sarah paints a sign shaped like a parallelogram. One angle is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
items.e: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°. The angle opposite the 70° angle is also 70°.

items.q: Sarah covers a bulletin board with congruent parallelogram tiles. One tile has sides of 4 cm and 7 cm. What is the perimeter of each tile?
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal: 4 + 7 + 4 + 7 = 22 cm. (28 is 4 × 7, not a perimeter.)

items.q: Priya sews 8 congruent rhombus patches for a quilt. Each side of one patch is 6 cm. How much ribbon does she need to go around all 8 patches?
items.e: One patch: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. The patches are congruent, so 8 patches need 8 × 24 = 192 cm.

items.q: Ethan measures a quadrilateral’s diagonals. Both are 10 cm, and they cut each other in half at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Equal diagonals that cut each other in half: rectangle. At right angles too: rhombus. Both: a square.

items.q: Dumisani makes a stained-glass design from 4 congruent kites placed around a centre point, each one a quarter turn from the next. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the design?
items.e: Each quarter turn moves every kite onto the next one, so the design fits onto itself 4 times in a full turn: order 4.

items.q: Lerato draws a quadrilateral. All 4 sides are 5 cm. Its diagonals are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. The diagonals are different lengths, so it is not a square. (Half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm make 5 cm sides.)

items.q: What is the red line called?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: The red line is part of this circle. What is it called?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: Which part of the circle is shown in red?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: What is the red line called?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: The red line is part of this circle. What is it called?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: Which part of the circle is shown in red?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: The edge of this circle is shown in red. What is it called?
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: What is the red part of this circle called?
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: What is the red point called?
items.e: The centre is the point in the middle. Every point on the circumference is the same distance from the centre.

items.q: The distance all the way round a circle is called the …
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 20 m. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 m.

items.q: What is the part marked in red called?
items.e: A diameter goes across the circle through the centre. Answer: the diameter.

items.q: What is the part marked in red called?
items.e: A radius goes from the centre to the edge. Answer: the radius.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 42 mm. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 42 ÷ 2 = 21 mm.

items.q: What is the part marked in red called?
items.e: The centre is the point in the middle of the circle. Answer: the centre.

items.q: What is the part marked in red called?
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the circle. Answer: the circumference.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 9 mm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: 2 × 9 = 18 mm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 52 mm. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 52 ÷ 2 = 26 mm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 11 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: 2 × 11 = 22 cm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 12 mm. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 mm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 4 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 7 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 2,5 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 2,5 = 5 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 12 mm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 12 = 24 mm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 15 m. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 15 = 30 m.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 10 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 18 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 9 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 9 ÷ 2 = 4,5 cm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 26 mm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 26 ÷ 2 = 13 mm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 3 m. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 3 ÷ 2 = 1,5 m.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3 cm. What is its diameter in millimetres?
items.e: Diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 cm = 60 mm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 9 cm. What is its radius in millimetres?
items.e: 9 cm = 90 mm. The radius is half the diameter: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 mm.

items.q: The circle fits exactly inside a square with sides of 10 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
items.e: The circle touches all 4 sides, so its diameter is the same as the side of the square: 10 cm. Radius = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: The circle has a radius of 6 cm and fits exactly inside the square. How long is each side of the square?
items.e: The side of the square is the same as the diameter of the circle: 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: A circle with a radius of 3 cm fits exactly inside a square. What is the perimeter of the square?
items.e: Each side of the square equals the diameter: 2 × 3 = 6 cm. Perimeter = 4 × 6 = 24 cm.

items.q: Two equal circles fit exactly inside the rectangle. Each circle has a radius of 4 cm. How long is the rectangle?
items.e: Each circle is 2 × 4 = 8 cm across. Two diameters: 8 + 8 = 16 cm.

items.q: Three equal circles fit exactly inside a rectangle 30 cm long. What is the radius of each circle?
items.e: The 3 diameters make 30 cm, so one diameter is 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm. Radius = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: A big circle has a radius of 12 cm. A small circle has a diameter that is the same length as the big circle’s radius. What is the radius of the small circle?
items.e: The small circle’s diameter is 12 cm, so its radius is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

items.q: Circle A has a radius of 7 cm. Circle B has a diameter of 12 cm. Which circle is wider, and by how much?
items.e: Compare diameters: A is 2 × 7 = 14 cm across and B is 12 cm across. 14 − 12 = 2 cm, so A is wider by 2 cm. Do not compare a radius with a diameter (7 with 12), and do not stop at the radii (7 − 6 = 1).

items.q: Which of these is true for every circle?
items.e: Two radii in a straight line through the centre make a diameter, so diameter = 2 × radius and radius = diameter ÷ 2.
